topic: Foundations of Linear Algebra: From Combinations to Bases

sections.title: The Ingredients: Linear Combinations and Span
lecture_lines: Scale two vectors to build combinations.
Combine them to sweep the plane.
All reachable points form the span.
Span is the set of all reaches.
animations: Fade in two vectors v1 (#FF5733) and v2 (#33FF57) at center.
Scale v1 and v2 with slider visuals and show linear combination v3 (#3357FF).
Animate parallelogram construction to shade the resulting area.
Show robot arm end-effector sweeping the entire shaded area.
Label the shaded area as 'Span' (#FFFFFF) with a glow effect.

sections.title: Redundancy: Linear Dependence
lecture_lines: Redundant vectors add no new reach.
They lie on the same line.
animations: Show three vectors v1, v2, v3 where v3 = v1 + v2.
Flash v3 in red (#FF0000) to signal it is linearly dependent.
Transform v3 into a dashed line to illustrate redundancy.

sections.title: Efficiency: The Basis
lecture_lines: Basis is the minimal spanning set.
Unique coordinates define every space point.
animations: Fade in a minimal set of two vectors (basis) for the 2D plane.
Animate a grid transformation where the grid lines align with the basis.
Color the basis vectors gold (#FFD700) and display 'Basis' text.

sections.title: Synthesis and Summary
animations: Fade in 'Span', 'Independence', and 'Basis' labels arranged in a circle.
Animate a light pulse traveling between the labels to connect them.
Merge the labels into a single 'Linear Algebra Foundation' text.
